en: The guests ate with a good appetite.
en_alt: The guests ate with appetite.
The guests ate heartily.
note: Bare "with appetite" is translationese; English says "with a good appetite".

en_alt: Please eat!
note: Same sentence without the comma is equally valid English.
Imperfective compound future correctly rendered "will be eating".

ru: В о́тпуске я бу́ду лежа́ть на пля́же и чита́ть.

en: Why are you lying down for so long?
en_alt: Why are you lying down so long?
Why have you been lying down so long?
note: English needs "for so long" after a durative present progressive.

ru: Он лежа́л в посте́ли весь день.
Я лежа́ла бы в гамаке́ весь день.
note: Imperfective бы+past as a present counterfactual "would lie" is right.

ru: Ещё два часа́ мы бу́дем лезть на верши́ну.
en_alt: We will be climbing to the summit for another two hours.
note: «на вершину» is "to the summit" as readily as "towards".

en_alt: I am climbing up the stairs.
note: «лестница» is glossed "stairs" corpus-wide and fits this sentence equally.

en_alt: The child is climbing up a tree.

ru: Ты бы не ле́зла на э́то де́рево.
en_alt: You would not climb that tree.
You'd better not climb that tree.
note: «Ты бы не …» with no condition clause is advisory, not a counterfactual; the bare "You would not climb that tree" reads as a stranded hypothetical.

ru: Ле́том я бу́ду лета́ть к мо́рю.
en_alt: In summer I will be flying to the sea.

ru: Я лета́ю в Москву́ ка́ждый год.
Е́сли бы не боя́лся, я лета́л бы ча́ще.
note: Imperfective present counterfactual "would fly" is correct.

en_alt: Do you fly a lot?

ru: До Пари́жа мы бу́дем лете́ть три часа́.
en: We will be flying to Paris for three hours.
en_alt: The flight to Paris will take us three hours.
note: The paraphrase drops the verb лететь entirely; the literal progressive is natural English and keeps the compound future visible.

en_alt: We are flying over the clouds.
I am treating a bad throat.

ru: Я лечи́л бы просту́ду ча́ем с мёдом.

note: Imperfective compound future correctly "will be treating".

ru: Ты бы легла́ пора́ньше, но мно́го рабо́ты.
en_alt: You would go to bed earlier, but there is a lot of work.
note: «но много работы» supplies the counterfactual, so the "would" reading holds; the bed idiom is an equally valid rendering.

en_alt: Will you go to bed?
note: «лечь спать» is ordinarily "go to bed"; the literal en_gb is kept for the gloss.

en_alt: I will go to bed a bit earlier.

ru: Сего́дня де́ти ля́гут спать в де́вять.
en_alt: Today the children will go to bed at nine.
She went to bed at ten.

note: «лишиться времени» is an odd collocation — лишиться normally takes a concrete possession or faculty (работы, голоса); a human should decide whether to reword the Russian.

ru: С рассве́та рыбаки́ бу́дут лови́ть ры́бу у бе́рега.
en_alt: From dawn the fishermen will be catching fish near the shore.
note: "fishing" is idiomatic but hides «ловить»; the literal reading is worth accepting.

en: The children were catching the ball in the meadow.
en_alt: The children were catching the ball on the meadow.
note: English is "in the meadow", not "on the meadow".

en_alt: The cat is catching a mouse.
Are you fishing?

ru: Я лови́л бы ба́бочек в саду́.
note: Frame collision with поймать, but this imperfective habitual "would catch" is the correct side; the perfective partner «Е́сли бы успе́л, я пойма́л бы мяч.» is the one that should read "I would have caught the ball if I had been in time."

en_alt: I am fishing in the river.

ru: Е́сли бы успева́л, я ложи́лся бы ра́ньше.
note: Imperfective habitual counterfactual; "would go to bed" is right.

ru: С за́втрашнего дня я бу́ду ложи́ться ра́но.
note: Compound future correctly "will be going to bed".

en_alt: We would lie down after dinner.
note: Habitual "would" is an equally valid reading of the imperfective past.

ru: Я не лома́ла бы чужи́е ве́щи.
note: Frame-only collision with сломать; the subjects, objects and polarity differ, so the contrast drill still has a cue, and both sides read correctly for their aspect.

en_alt: They were pulling down the old house.

ru: За́втра рабо́чие бу́дут лома́ть ста́рый дом.
en_alt: Tomorrow the workers will be pulling down the old house.
The wind is breaking the branches of the trees.
The man who loved her went away.
We loved walking in the park.
She loves her work.
note: «работа» is glossed "work"; both renderings are natural.

ru: Ты бы люби́ла э́тот го́род бо́льше без шу́ма.

en_alt: Do you love classical music?

note: Frame collision with полюбить is only nominal — the partner sentences read "came to love", which already distinguishes the perfective.

ru: Я всегда́ бу́ду люби́ть свою́ семью́.
note: Stative verb, so the compound future is correctly a plain "will love", not "will be loving".
Frame collision with полюбить is harmless: the partners read "came to love".

en_alt: The children were waving small flags.
Are you waving little flags?
note: Russian has no article, so the indefinite reading is equally valid.

ru: С э́того дня я бу́ду маха́ть тебе́ с перро́на.
Я маха́ла бы фла́гом гро́мче всех.
note: «махать флагом громче всех» is an odd collocation (гро́мче belongs with noise verbs); the English mirrors the oddity, so a human should decide whether to reword the Russian.

ru: Е́сли бы заме́тил тебя́, я махну́л бы руко́й.
en: I would have waved my hand if I had noticed you.
en_alt: I would have waved if I had noticed you.
note: «рукой» is dropped; the sibling sentence renders it "his hand", so keep it here too. Perfective "would have waved" is already right.

en_alt: Will you wave your handkerchief?
note: "give a wave" marks the semelfactive but the plain verb is what most speakers would write.

en_alt: She waved her handkerchief.

note: Idiomatic and accurate for the У-меня possessive frame.

ru: Без све́та ничего́ бы не мелькну́ло.
note: Perfective бы+past correctly rendered "would have flashed".
Stress mark is wrong: nominative plural of тень is те́ни; тени́ is the locative singular (в тени́).

ru: Я не меня́ла бы рабо́ту так ча́сто.
В выходны́е мы бу́дем меня́ть ле́тние ши́ны.

en_alt: Do you change money?
Are you changing money at the bank?
I am changing money at the bank.
She is trying on a dress at the shop.
She dreams of a journey.
She dreams about a trip.
note: «путешествие» is glossed "journey"; "travelling" loses the noun.

en_alt: Do you dream of a journey?
Do you dream about a trip?
What do you dream of?

ru: В де́тстве он мечта́л стать лётчиком.
en_alt: In childhood he dreamed of becoming a pilot.
Do you dream about a house?
The children dream about the holidays.

ru: Я всегда́ бу́ду мечта́ть о мо́ре.
note: Stative verb, so the plain "will always dream" is right for the compound future.

en_alt: I dream about a new house.

ru: Я не меша́ла бы тебе́ рабо́тать.
en_alt: I would not disturb you while you work.
I would not stop you working.

note: The translation is right, but мешать here means "to stir", which the headword gloss "to hinder" does not cover — the gloss is likely the half that needs widening.
Same "to stir" sense as the sibling sentence; the headword gloss "to hinder" does not cover it.

en_alt: Don't disturb your sister!
Don't bother your sister!
The noise stops me from working.
The noise keeps me from working.
note: "hinders me from working" is stiff but keeps the gloss visible; the natural variants should be accepted.

en: The noise will stop us from sleeping.
en_alt: The noise will keep us from sleeping.
The noise will be hindering our sleep.
note: "will be hindering our sleep" is translationese and also recasts «нам спать» as a noun phrase.

ru: Без уда́чи беда́ не минова́ла бы нас.
note: Perfective бы+past correctly rendered "would not have passed".

en_alt: The car will pass the village.
note: миновать is biaspectual, so минует reads as future perfective just as readily.

en_alt: The train will pass the station without stopping.

ru: Ве́чером она́ бу́дет моли́ться о здоро́вье.

en: He prayed before going to sleep.
en_alt: He prayed before bed.
He prayed before sleep.
note: Bare "before sleep" is not idiomatic English for «перед сном».

ru: Я моли́лась бы за тебя́ ка́ждый день.

en_alt: They pray in the church.

ru: Не ка́ждый мо́жет рабо́тать по ноча́м.
en_alt: Not everyone can work at night.
They could not find the road.

ru: Е́сли бы был свобо́ден, я мог бы помо́чь.

en_alt: Are you rushing along the street?
note: "racing" drifts from the headword gloss "to rush", which the sibling sentences use.

ru: Ты бы мча́лся домо́й быстре́е ве́тра.

en_alt: The cars were rushing along the highway.
